newsitem.title: NIGERIA: OIL MARKETERS DOWN AS NIGERIA BOURSE FALLS FURTHER.
newsitem.headline: OIL MARKETERS DOWN AS NIGERIA BOURSE FALLS FURTHER.

text.p: Oil marketing shares were the big losers in Wednesday trade on the Nigerian stock exchange as pressure to sell showed no signs of relenting, dealers said.
The all-share index dropped to 8061.92 from 8089.72 on Tuesday.
"More sellers were flooding the market to offload the shares. They see no better prospects in the offing soon," one trader said.
Unipetrol shares were down 40 kobo at 63.00 naira and African Petroleum dropped 20 kobo to 49.30 naira as a consequence.
Agip shares closed 20 kobo down at 14.10 naira while Total was at 54.80 naira, five kobo lower. Texaco slid five kobo to 37.60 naira.
A surprise drop in profits at UBA, one of the leading banks, cost its shares 40 kobo and it closed at 12.50 naira.
Selling pressure further depressed food shares.
Nigerian Bottling Company lost 20 kobo at 49.50 naira and Cadbury was 32.90 naira, down 10 kobo.
Conglomerates fared no better. PZ Industries ended 40 kobo lower at 23.60 naira, Lever Brothers dropped 20 kobo to 23.60 naira and UAC ended at 13.50 naira, down 15 kobo.
On the gainers side, AIICO Insurance continued to impress dealers, adding 50 kobo at 16.50 naira.
NAL Merchant Bank, which also posted good full year results recently, closed 19 kobo higher at 9.80 naira.
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham continued its current upswing to end at 5.65 naira, ending 10 kobo higher.
United Textiles rose a similar 10 kobo to 6.10 naira.
